name: Aiah
overview: Aiah is a male biblical figure known primarily as the father of Rizpah. There is no record of his tribal affiliation or additional personal details in Scripture. His mention is brief and serves mainly to identify his daughter within the biblical narrative.
namesAndTitles: The name Aiah means "black kite," a proper name noted in 2 Samuel 3:7. This name is not indicated as being given directly by God, and no further titles are associated with him in Scripture.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Aiah as the father of Rizpah. Beyond this paternal relationship, no other family connections or relationships are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Aiah's significance in the biblical narrative lies in his identification as the father of Rizpah, a figure connected to important events in 2 Samuel. While Aiah himself does not play an active role in the story, his mention provides necessary genealogical context that helps trace Rizpah's lineage, contributing to the historical and familial framework of the biblical account.
